data.translation: The person himself is everything. Until one side becomes water, they calm down with one another... And if not, it is finished... That is the possibility for this reconciliation, for this peace, Jan!

rationale: First I Infectum example for the figurative subsense; reciprocal softening situated in reconciliation.

summary: All 13 records were checked. Infectum-wa grukxowa describes the cheese-softening process; Preterit-wa rakixowa in the following verse presents achieved softness anterior to pressing. Both are already in the entry and are not re-added.

Part act. rakixo can be predicative with a copula, attributive to cotton, and part of a coordinated property description. Feminine rakәxto is retained in this inherited category. These static forms must not be classified as Preterit from the English or German tense alone.
The inherited wording “would be great to know why the [k] is plosive” is preserved as a question. The orphan “Preterit Intransitive” is structural metadata, not a newly attested finite example.
No Detransitive formation is shown. I is already intransitive, whereas III has a body or person as patient; a stative adjective does not imply a Detransitive derivation.
Round 1 already broadened I.1 to weich sein, weich werden. The empty Preterit Intransitive heading was not an attestation: Jan now supplies finite rakəx with road and heart subjects.

Figurative I.1b complements the already inherited figurative III erweichen; it does not duplicate the III sense. The Turoyo calming/pleasing paraphrases and ṣəlḥo/šayno discourse support emotional yielding.
rakəx in these finite contexts is distinct from the rakixo/rakəxto property forms filed as Part act. in round 1. No Detransitive is inferred from intransitive change.
Jan English is the project machine translation, not an edition translation. It is reproduced only as supplied and is not evidence for senses; all semantic decisions rest on the Turoyo.
